primary_task: Test a local web application by starting its dev server and running a Python Playwright script in headless Chromium that navigates, inspects the DOM and takes a screenshot.

requirements.name: python
requirements.evidence: To test local web applications, write native Python Playwright scripts.
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "run shell commands on Linux x86_64: ... build, test, run CLIs and scripts"; Python is standard software of the Linux platform and installable via apt from Ubuntu

requirements.name: playwright (Python package)
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads)"

requirements.name: chromium browser binary
requirements.evidence: browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True) # Always launch chromium in headless mode
requirements.basis: The manifest does not say whether a Chromium build is present or where Playwright downloads it from; egress_allow covers PyPI, npm, GitHub and Ubuntu archives only. Check whether `playwright install chromium` reaches its download host, or whether a Chromium from apt can be used.

requirements.name: local web server
requirements.evidence: python scripts/with_server.py --server "npm run dev" --port 5173 -- python your_automation.py
requirements.basis: grants: "local_servers"; tools.bash: "start and stop local servers inside the session"

requirements.name: scripts/with_server.py
requirements.evidence: **Helper Scripts Available**: - `scripts/with_server.py` - Manages server lifecycle (supports multiple servers)
requirements.basis: The manifest does not say which skill files are present; check that the skill's scripts/ folder is installed with the skill.

requirements.name: npm
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, ...)"

notes: Unknown: the Chromium browser binary Playwright needs (the document does not say how it is obtained; if its download host is refused and no apt Chromium works, the task would be BLOCKED), and the presence of the bundled with_server.py helper (the server can also be started by hand, so not hard). npm is needed only if the app under test is an npm project.
